question: How does the lymphatic system differ mainly from the blood circulation system?

options.A: A high-pressure pumping network powered directly by the heart
options.B: A closed-loop system carrying oxygenated blood to all deep tissues
options.C: A solid structural barrier preventing any fluid movement between tissues
options.D: A low-pressure drainage network that collects excess interstitial fluid

explanation: The lymphatic system works as a low-pressure drainage network to gather fluid that escapes from blood capillaries into body tissues. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h1)

question: What happens if the lymphatic system fails to collect fluid from the spaces between tissues?

options.A: Blood pressure in the main arteries would immediately drop to zero
options.B: Red blood cells would rapidly multiply inside the body tissues
options.C: Nutrients would stop reaching the cells through the bloodstream
options.D: Tissue fluid would build up and cause severe swelling called edema

explanation: Uncollected interstitial fluid accumulates rapidly in tissues when lymphatic drainage fails, leading to the clinical condition of edema. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h1)

question: What is the specialized name for lipid-rich lymph that drains from the digestive tract?
explanation: Chyle is the milky, fat-laden lymph collected from the lacteals in the small intestine during fat digestion. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h2)

question: Why do large plasma proteins enter lymphatic capillaries instead of returning straight to blood capillaries?

options.A: Venous capillary walls are too tightly sealed for large proteins to re-enter
options.B: Lymphatic vessels actively destroy plasma proteins to create energy
options.C: Proteins prefer to circulate inside lymph nodes rather than in blood plasma
options.D: Blood capillaries only allow solid mineral waste products to pass through

explanation: Large proteins slip easily through the highly permeable walls of initial lymphatics, but they cannot cross back into the tight junctions of blood capillaries. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h2)

question: Which feature of initial lymphatic capillaries stops fluid from leaking backward into the tissues?
explanation: The endothelial cells of lymphatic capillaries overlap loosely, creating one-way valve flaps that open with outside pressure and seal shut with inside pressure. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h3)

question: In what order does lymph flow as it travels upward through the vessels?

options.A: Capillaries -> Collecting vessels -> Lymph trunks -> Lymphatic ducts
options.B: Lymph trunks -> Capillaries -> Collecting vessels -> Lymphatic ducts
options.C: Lymphatic ducts -> Collecting vessels -> Capillaries -> Lymph trunks
options.D: Collecting vessels -> Lymphatic ducts -> Capillaries -> Lymph trunks

explanation: Lymph originates in microscopic capillaries, moves into larger collecting vessels, passes through trunks, and finally reaches the large lymphatic ducts before joining the blood. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h3)

question: Which specific zone of a lymph node contains primarily T-lymphocytes?
explanation: The paracortex houses the T-cell rich zone of the lymph node, positioned right between the superficial cortex and the central medulla. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h4)

question: What is the function of the germinal centers found within the cortical follicles of a lymph node?

options.A: They pump lymph fluid through the node using rhythmic muscle contractions
options.B: They produce and multiply B-lymphocytes during an active immune response
options.C: They physically block red blood cells from entering the lymphatic ducts
options.D: They store excess water and mineral salts for emergency hydration

explanation: Germinal centers act as active sites where B-lymphocytes proliferate and differentiate into antibody-producing plasma cells when fighting infection. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h4)

question: What type of vessel carries unfiltered lymph INTO a lymph node?
explanation: Afferent vessels approach and enter the lymph node, while efferent vessels carry filtered lymph away from the node. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h5)

question: Why do lymph nodes swell and feel tender during a local bacterial infection?

options.A: Excess water leaks from the node capsule directly into the skin layers
options.B: The efferent vessels permanently close to trap bacteria forever
options.C: Blood clots form inside the lymphatic ducts to block the infection
options.D: Lymphocytes and immune cells multiply rapidly inside the node to fight invaders

explanation: Rapid proliferation of immune cells and heightened activity inside the node during an immune response cause the node to enlarge and feel tender. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h5)

question: Which major lymphatic duct drains the lower body and the entire left side of the upper body?
explanation: The thoracic duct is the largest lymphatic vessel in the body, collecting lymph from both lower limbs, the abdomen, and the left upper body quadrant. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h6)

question: How do skeletal muscles help move lymph through the deep vessels?

options.A: Muscles pull directly on the lymph node capsules to empty their contents
options.B: Muscles release heat that turns lymph into a gas for easier travel
options.C: Contracting muscles compress the lymph vessels, pushing fluid past one-way valves
options.D: Skeletal muscles pump blood directly into the initial lymphatic capillaries

explanation: The skeletal muscle pump squeezes surrounding lymph vessels during movement, driving lymph upward through the one-way internal valves. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h6)
